port.name: Gemini CLI
port.description: Living Code for Gemini CLI: standalone custom theme files for conversational text, borders, status indicators and diff backgrounds.

guide.installation:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/living-code-theme/gemini-cli.git
cd gemini-cli
```

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.gemini/themes"
cp themes/*.json "$HOME/.gemini/themes/"
printf "%s\n" "$HOME/.gemini/themes/living-code-night.json"
```

Copy the printed absolute path into `ui.theme` in your existing `~/.gemini/settings.json`, preserving all other settings. Example shape:

```json
{
  "ui": {
    "theme": "/home/you/.gemini/themes/living-code-night.json"
  }
}
```

Replace `/home/you` with your actual home directory, then restart Gemini CLI.
guide.configuration: The distributable files are standalone `type: "custom"` theme documents, not full settings files. As an alternative, insert a document into `ui.customThemes` using its `name` as the object key, then select it by name. A path selected through `ui.theme` must be removed before changing themes with `/theme`.
guide.compatibility: Uses the documented standalone-file custom theme API. Gemini CLI permits theme paths only within the home directory: do not point it at a clone under `/tmp` or a system-wide location. Text, background, diff, border, status and UI groups are provided; code highlighting follows Gemini CLI’s derived theme behavior. Tests validate the nested format, not provider access or model output.
